           /\ Conn(c, Store)
           /\ \E Q \in SUBSET Nodes :
                /\ Majority(Q)
                /\ \A q \in Q : up[q] /\ Conn(q, Store) /\ Conn(q, c)
                /\ \A q, r \in Q : Conn(q, r)

\* derives: C1.4 -- if the good condition eventually holds forever, every pending
\* requester eventually stops waiting (obtains a grant)
C1_4 == \A c \in Clients : (<>[]Good(c)) => [](pending[c] => <>(~pending[c]))

\* derives: C1.1, C1.4 -- bound check: no election ever reaches the last allowed term,
\* so MaxTerm never constrains a behaviour (run.sh reports a violation as UNEXPLAINED)
TermHeadroom == \A n \in Nodes : promised[n] < MaxTerm

\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3 -- witness target: the run ended and the system is quiescent
\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3; format v2 E1 -- quiescent: no request, write or ack in flight
\* and no client waiting for a grant, with crashed and paused processes not counted
\* (a message counts as in flight when its receiver is running)
Active(c) == up[c] /\ ~paused[c]
\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3; format v2 E1
Quiescent == /\ \A m \in grantMsgs : ~Active(m.c)
             /\ writeMsgs = {} \/ ~up[Store]
             /\ \A a \in ackMsgs : ~Active(a.c)
             /\ \A a \in toAck : ~up[Store] \/ ~Active(a.c)
             /\ \A c \in Clients : Active(c) => ~pending[c]
             /\ readMsgs = {} \/ ~up[Store]                      \* derives: C2.1; format v2 E1
             /\ \A a \in rAckMsgs : ~Active(a.c)                  \* derives: C2.2; format v2 E1
             /\ \A a \in rToAck : ~up[Store] \/ ~Active(a.c)      \* derives: C2.2; format v2 E1
\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3; format v2 E1 -- the run has reached its end: every step applied,
\* and either the end trigger fired (armed when the last step was taken) or, for
\* `end: quiescent`, the state is quiescent
Done == /\ pc = Len(Steps) + 1
        /\ IF EndTrig.event = "quiescent" THEN Quiescent ELSE fired
\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3 -- violated by any trace that reaches the end of the schedule
NotEnded == ~(Done /\ Quiescent)
\* derives: F1.1, F1.2, F1.3 -- weaker witness: the schedule's end trigger fired
NotDone == ~Done
=============================================================================

# Model-side predictions, X2 adapt arm (failure model v2: partial and simplex partitions)

derives: C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, C1.4, C2.1, C2.2, F1.1, F1.2, F1.3, F2.1, F2.2; format v4 (cut, drop, L1-L3, E1, E3, T3); observe v4 addendum; pairs v3 (P1-P30)

Additive. The earlier prediction files are not edited. Committed after reading the X2 brief, `contract/v2.md`, `failure-model/v2.md`, `tests/pairs-v3.md`, the format v4 addendum, the observe v4 addendum, the 31 shared schedules and this directory, and before any change to the model or any TLC run in this arm. Scoring is unchanged: a schedule's verdict is the one line `run.sh` prints; a mutation counts as working only if it prints `FAIL <its clause>`.

## Plan, fixed before predicting
- **Links replace sides.** `sideA` (one side of a bipartition) cannot express F2.1 or F2.2. It is replaced by `down`, the set of directed links that are down. `Link(p, q)` means p→q is up. `Conn(p, q)`, "connected", becomes both directions of the direct link up (failure model v2). F1.2 `partition` adds every crossing pair in both directions; `cut` adds each listed pair in both directions; `drop` adds each listed pair in the listed direction; any `heal` empties `down` (L2).
- **A message's fate is fixed when it is sent.** Every send checks the one directed link it uses, at the moment of sending: a write or read checks client→storage, an ack checks storage→client. A message already in flight is no longer dropped when a link goes down. This contradicts my v1 interpretation 13 (a partition dropped in-flight messages whose endpoints ended up on different sides).
- **The abstract grantor, link by link.**
  - Hearing a leader is directional: node n hears leader m iff m→n is up. `Elect(n)` needs that n hears no current leader.
  - A vote and a grant confirmation are round trips, so the quorum members must be connected to the candidate or leader (both directions).
  - **Voter stickiness (new).** A node votes only if it hears no current leader itself (a pre-vote check). Under v1 this is a no-op in every case that matters: a node that cannot hear the leader is on the far side of a bipartition, and so is every node it can reach. Under F2.1 it is what keeps the cut-off follower in P19 and P25 from disrupting a grantor that still has a majority. Without it, elections through the middle node can cycle, and the term bound would end the run as UNEXPLAINED.
  - **Quorum check (new, `CheckQuorum(n)`).** A leader that is not connected to a majority (itself included) steps down. Under F2.2 (P20, P26) the followers still hear a grantor that cannot hear them, so without this nobody would ever elect.
  - `StepDown(n)` needs to hear the node with the higher promise (q→n up). `Join(n, q)` needs only n→q.
  - `Grant(n, c)` is taken only when n and c are connected. A grant sent into a down link is not modelled (interpretation in the README).
- **C1.4's premise (L3).** `Good(c)`: storage and c are up, c is not paused, c and storage are connected, and some majority Q of up lease nodes is pairwise connected and connected to storage and to c. Under v1 bipartitions this is equivalent to the old `Good(c)`.
- **Fairness.** The same weak fairness as before, plus `WF(CheckQuorum(n))`. The README will name every condition and its justification under the brief's rule.
- **Compiler.** `cut` (F2.1), `drop` (F2.2), `heal` under F1.2, F2.1 and F2.2. Selectors `grantor`, `holder`, `non-grantor` are allowed in a link; `rest` is rejected (L1). Self-pairs are dropped at run time (L1). `MaxTerm` counts `cut` and `drop` steps as fault steps.
- **Exporter.** A `cut` or `drop` Fault record carries `links`, the directed links taken down after resolving selectors and removing self-pairs. Every heal record carries `links: []` and `heal: true`.

## Schedules (31)
| Schedule | Predicted | Note |
|---|---|---|
| P1 .. P18 | PASS | Removing in-flight drops only removes behaviours, so safety cannot newly fail. Stickiness and CheckQuorum change no v1 liveness outcome. State counts will change. |
| false-suspicion-v1 | PASS | |
| P19 | PASS | One leader throughout. Stickiness keeps the cut-off follower from electing through the middle node. |
| P20 | PASS | The grantor steps down by CheckQuorum; n2 or n3 is elected and grants. |
| P21 | PASS | The cut grantor cannot confirm; the other two elect; c1's stale write is rejected. |
| P22 | PASS | |
| P23 | PASS | c1 may still be told v1 succeeded, if the ack was sent before the cut; v1 was accepted, so that is not a violation. |
| P24 | PASS | |
| P25 | PASS | The grantor keeps its majority with the middle node (Join if needed); the cut-off follower cannot elect. |
| P26 | PASS | Depends on CheckQuorum under weak fairness. Without it, this would be FAIL C1_4. |
| P27 | PASS | |
| P28 | PASS | |
| P29 | PASS | As P23: a read ack sent before the cut may still be delivered. |
| P30 | PASS | |

## Mutations (30)
**P1-P18.** Unchanged breaks, re-applied mechanically. `Restart` replacements name `down` instead of `sideA`. P18's anchor changes from `Conn(Store, a.c)` to `Link(Store, a.c)`. P8, P11 and P17 keep `Conn`, which now means "connected"; on their bipartition schedules this is the same as before. Predicted as before: P1-P3 `FAIL C1_1`, P4-P6 `FAIL C1_2`, P7-P9 `FAIL C1_3`, P10-P12 `FAIL C1_4`, P13-P15 `FAIL C2_1`, P16-P18 `FAIL C2_2`.

**New mutations, named here before running:**
| Mutation | Break (on the clause's enforcing path) | Predicted |
|---|---|---|
| P19 | A voter that still hears the leader lends its vote to a candidate without promising the new term (a pre-vote counted as a vote). The cut-off follower is elected through the middle node, which stays promised to the old term. The old grantor keeps confirming grants through it, and once the new leader brings the middle node into its term, it grants from a stale token. | FAIL C1_1 |
| P20 | A newly elected leader starts from its own durable `maxTok`, not the highest over its quorum. On P20 the only leadership change is the one the F2.2 step-down causes. Not specific to F2.2, like P3. | FAIL C1_1 |
| P21 | Storage defers to a grantor it can still reach: it accepts a token below the ledger when the node that issued it is connected to storage and still believes it leads. On P21 the cut grantor reaches storage and may not yet have stepped down. | FAIL C1_2 |
| P22 | Storage keeps the fence per client (the highest token accepted from that writer), not per key. The old holder, which hears no lease node, presents its own old token. Not specific to F2.2. | FAIL C1_2 |
| P23 | A client that has lost only its storage link, and still reaches a lease node, presumes its outstanding writes succeeded. This is v1's transitive reasoning: a real partition would have cut it from the lease nodes too. | FAIL C1_3 |
| P24 | A client that can send to storage but hears nothing back presumes its outstanding writes succeeded, possibly before storage decides. | FAIL C1_3 |
| P25 | The grantor will not grant while any lease node is unreachable: it waits for the whole configuration. Under F2.1, progress depends on the majority sufficing. | FAIL C1_4 |
| P26 | CheckQuorum counts the followers the grantor can send to, not the ones it is connected to. The P26 grantor therefore never steps down, the followers keep hearing it, and nobody elects. | FAIL C1_4 |
| P27 | The read counterpart of P21: storage serves a read below the ledger when the token's grantor is connected to storage and still believes it leads. | FAIL C2_1 |
| P28 | The read counterpart of P22: storage fences reads per client. | FAIL C2_1 |
| P29 | A client that has lost only its storage link, and still reaches a lease node, answers its outstanding read from its cache: the value it last read, or `"none"` if it has read nothing. | FAIL C2_2 |
| P30 | A client that can send to storage but hears nothing back presumes its outstanding read was served, with the value of the last write it was told succeeded, possibly before storage serves it. | FAIL C2_2 |

**Risks named before running.**
- **P19's mutation may print UNEXPLAINED (MaxTerm bound) instead of FAIL C1_1.** The mutated voters also let elections cycle. TLC stops at the first violated invariant in breadth-first order, so if the term bound is reached at a shallower depth than the duplicate token, the run is UNEXPLAINED. I expect the duplicate token at a depth of about 7 after the cut, and the bound needs about 5 more elections of about 3 steps each.

    /\ UNCHANGED rvars  \* derives: C2.1, C2.2 -- reads untouched

    /\ maxTok' = IF p \in Nodes THEN [maxTok EXCEPT ![p] = 0] ELSE maxTok \* mutation: P1

                   toAck, grants, rq, issued, decisions, told>>
    /\ lastEv' = [event |-> "Fault", cell |-> "F1.1", action |-> "restart", target |-> p]
""")]),

def replace_def(src, name, new):
    # derives: P1, P4, P7, P13 -- replace the definition block of `name` (with its comments)
    lines = src.split("\n")
    start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if re.match(rf"^{name}(\(| ==)", l))
    while start > 0 and lines[start - 1].startswith("\\*"):
        start -= 1
    end = start
    while end < len(lines) and lines[end].strip() != "":
        end += 1
    return "\n".join(lines[:start] + new.rstrip("\n").split("\n") + lines[end:])


def build(pair, derives, desc, edits, src):
    # derives: P1-P30 (pairs v3; was tagged P1-P12 only, stale since X1, fixed in the routing round)
    for kind, a, b in edits:
        if kind == "def":
            src = replace_def(src, a, b)
        else:
            n = src.count(a)
            if n != 1:
                raise SystemExit(f"{pair}: anchor occurs {n} times: {a!r}")
            src = src.replace(a, b)
    head, rest = src.split("\n", 1)
    return (head + f"\n\\* mutation: {pair} {desc}\n\\* derives: {pair}, {derives}\n" + rest)

    src = (HERE / "Lease.tla").read_text()

        d = HERE / "mutations" / pair

        (d / "Lease.tla").write_text(build(pair, derives, desc, edits, src))

Additive. The earlier prediction files are not edited. Committed after reading the X3 brief, `contract/v3.md`, `failure-model/v3.md`, `tests/pairs-v4.md`, `testbed/schedule-format.md` (v5 addendum included), `observe/schema.md` (v5 addendum included), `observe/decision_replay.py` and its test traces, the 59 shared schedules and this directory, and before any change to the model. One TLC run was made before this file: unmodified P5, to check that the toolchain at `/opt/tlaplus/tla2tools.jar` works (PASS, 5,561 distinct states, as in X2). It informs nothing below.

Scoring is as before: a schedule's verdict is the one line `run.sh` prints; a mutation counts as working only if it prints `FAIL <its clause>`.

## Plan, fixed before predicting

**Protocol followed.** Raft with joint consensus for membership change (Ongaro and Ousterhout, "In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm", USENIX ATC 2014, section 6; Ongaro, "Consensus: Bridging Theory and Practice", PhD thesis, Stanford, 2014, chapter 4, section 4.3), at the level of abstraction the previous author's model already used for elections and grants: a leader per term, a majority promising the term, the new leader adopting the most recent state of its quorum, and a grant decided atomically with the majority's agreement. Amnesia (F3.3) follows the rule that a replica that lost its disk must not vote until it has been brought back by the protocol (Chandra, Griesemer and Redstone, "Paxos Made Live: An Engineering Perspective", PODC 2007, section 5.1, "disk corruption"), expressed as Raft's non-voting member (thesis 4.2.1) and the contract's re-admission. Adaptations to the contract are listed in the README when done; the main ones are fixed now:
- A configuration change is one atomic decision counted by eligible majorities of the old and the new configuration (Raft commits C_old,new and then C_new; the contract's commit of e+1 is the first, and the model takes the second to follow at once). Every node that agreed keeps the proposal durably, which is what makes a later leader of either configuration adopt it.
- A node's election, grant and commit quorums count only **eligible** members (the contract's definition), with the whole membership as denominator. An amnesic incarnation votes and agrees in no counted quorum until a commit re-admits it; it may agree to a configuration that lists it, recorded with `counted_toward: []`.
- A node agrees to a configuration only after it has caught up to the leader's configuration history (Raft's catch-up of new servers, thesis 4.2.1).
- A request targets the epoch after its receiver's current one when it is recorded; another commit of that epoch supersedes it (C3.4).
- The grantor still does not wait for expiry (interpretation 3, now explicitly allowed by contract v3, "Lifetime"). No recorded decision reads a clock.

**Clocks (F3.2).** Each process has a clock offset (environment state, changed only by `clock` steps). A forward step on a lease node may fire its timers early: it may then stand for election, vote, or (as leader) give up its quorum, although it hears a leader. A backward step only delays timers, which the model's untimed failure detector already allows, so it changes nothing that is enabled. No protocol decision of the unmutated model reads the offset; some mutations do.

The v1 reading of C1.1 (tokens increase along the model's total order) is kept as a non-clause check whose violation prints `UNEXPLAINED`.
**Mutation runs check the pair's own clause** (with `TypeOK` and the bound check). Reason, found while designing: under v3 a grant without a majority (P2's break) violates C3.7 in the very state it is issued, before any token repeats, so with every clause checked P2's mutation would print `FAIL C3_7`. The question a mutation pair asks is whether the check of its clause catches the break; I will also say, where I know it, which other clause the break violates. For the C3.5 pairs, `observe/decision_replay.py` is run on the counterexample trace together with the unmutated witness of the same schedule, and must report it.

## Schedules (59)
| Schedule | Predicted | Note |
|---|---|---|
| P1-P30, false-suspicion-v1, H7-H10 | PASS | No reconfiguration, clock step or amnesia. The added clauses hold trivially or by construction; v3's C1.1 reading is weaker than the v1 reading the model already passed. State counts will change (event bookkeeping). |
| P31 | PASS | One of r1/r2 commits epoch 1; the other is superseded, or commits epoch 2 if its receiver records it after learning epoch 1. r3 refused `invalid`. Risk: state space (5 nodes, up to two commits) and `MaxTerm` headroom. |
| P32 | PASS | The backward step changes nothing enabled. |
| P33 | PASS | r2 at amnesic n3 targets epoch 1 (superseded) or epoch 2 if n3 has learned epoch 1 first. |
| P40 | PASS | C3.4(b): n1 and n2 commit with n4 or n5; if n3 was grantor it gives up its quorum. |
| P41 | PASS | Backward steps only. |
| P42 | PASS | n3 is ineligible; n1, n2 (and n4) suffice. |
| P43 | PASS | |
| P44 | PASS | Forward step may fire the grantor's quorum timer: a spurious step-down and re-election, harmless to safety. |
| P45 | PASS | The commit of r1 records n2#1's agreement in some behaviours and not in others; `readmits` follows. |
| P46 | PASS | New members catch up (learn epoch 0's history), agree with the inherited token count, elect among themselves. Risk: 6 nodes. |
| P47 | PASS | |
| P48 | PASS | Any 3 remaining eligible members intersect c1's grant quorum. |
| P49 | PASS | |
| P50 | PASS | The client's clock decides nothing. |
| P51 | PASS | |
| P52 | PASS | Risk: 6 nodes; liveness through the new configuration's election. |
| P53 | PASS | |
| P54 | PASS | |
| P58 | PASS | The grant is atomic in this model, so "c2's grant and the change in progress together" is not explored: the trigger `Agreed` fires on c2's grant step. Named as a limitation. |
| P59 | PASS | |
| P60 | PASS | |
| P61 | PASS | n4 forwards r1 through n2 or n3 (one hop); r2 is refused `busy` at n4 or recorded at n3. |
| P62 | PASS | |
| P63 | PASS | |

**P1-P30.** The breaks are unchanged and re-applied mechanically to the new text (anchors and `UNCHANGED` frames follow the model). Predicted as before: P1-P3, P19, P20 `FAIL C1_1`; P4-P6, P21, P22 `FAIL C1_2`; P7-P9, P23, P24 `FAIL C1_3`; P10-P12, P25, P26 `FAIL C1_4`; P13-P15, P27, P28 `FAIL C2_1`; P16-P18, P29, P30 `FAIL C2_2`.

| Pair | Break | Predicted |
|---|---|---|
| P31 | The decider does not apply its own commit to its configuration history (it records the decision, but keeps proposing from the old epoch), so a second pending request for the same epoch is committed too. | FAIL C3_1 |
| P32 | The leader numbers the new configuration from its clock: next epoch = current + 1 + its clock offset in lifetimes (rounded towards zero), so after the backward step the number it decides is not above the current epoch. | FAIL C3_1 |
| P33 | A leader accepts a forwarded request at whatever epoch the receiver targeted, counting it against its own current configuration; an amnesic receiver that has not learned epoch 1 targets epoch 1 again. | FAIL C3_1 |
| P40 | The leader waits for agreements from every member of the old configuration before it commits; the partitioned follower never agrees. | FAIL C3_4 |
| P41 | A leader whose clock reads earlier than its own clock when it recorded a request treats the request as a replay and silently drops it, while the receiver keeps it pending. | FAIL C3_4 |
| P42 | The leader will not commit while any member of the old configuration is in an incarnation not yet re-admitted (it waits for a re-admission r1 does not perform). | FAIL C3_4 |
| P43 | The decider drops from the new membership every requested member it cannot reach (it consults its links, which it does not record): the commit's members differ from its recorded `requested_members`. | FAIL C3_5; replay reports it |
| P44 | Storage judges a write or read expired by its own clock, which it does not record; since elapsed run time is open in the model (F3.2), any write or read may be judged expired and rejected. | FAIL C3_5; replay reports it |
| P45 | The decider puts in `readmits` every amnesic incarnation in the new membership that it can reach, not only those whose agreement it recorded. | FAIL C3_5; replay reports it |
| P46 | The nodes agreeing to a configuration commit do not receive the leader's token count (no log transfer with the joint entry), so the new configuration's first leader starts from 0. | FAIL C1_1 |
| P47 | The grantor takes its next token from its clock: max(1, last + 1 + its clock offset in lifetimes); after the backward step it reissues an old token. | FAIL C1_1 |
| P48 | An amnesic restart keeps the node's incarnation number (treated as an ordinary restart), so its empty state votes and agrees as if it were the old node. | FAIL C1_1 |
| P49 | Storage resets its ledger to 0 whenever a configuration commit is decided (a new configuration treated as a new fencing era). | FAIL C1_2 |
| P50 | Storage accepts a stale write if the writer's own clock says its grant is unexpired (its clock offset is negative). | FAIL C1_2 |
| P51 | Storage fails open: while some lease node is in an incarnation not yet re-admitted, it accepts every write without comparing it to the ledger. | FAIL C1_2 |
| P52 | Only members of the deployment's initial configuration may stand for election, so a configuration that replaced them all never elects. | FAIL C1_4 |
| P53 | A lease node whose clock has stepped refuses to agree to grants (a clock alarm nobody clears); every node steps, so no majority agrees after the last step. | FAIL C1_4 |
| P54 | The leader suspends granting while any member of its configuration is in an incarnation not yet re-admitted (nobody requests the re-admission). | FAIL C1_4 |
| P58 | The grantor issues every grant under the deployment's initial configuration and does not give up leadership when a commit removes it, so after the commit it grants under epoch 0 although its current configuration is epoch 1. | FAIL C3_7 |
| P59 | The leader counts as a member any node whose clock is ahead of its own (a membership table refreshed by heartbeats stamped with the sender's clock), so after its forward step the removed n3 is counted toward epoch 1's majority. | FAIL C3_7 |
| P60 | Grant counting ignores incarnations: an amnesic incarnation's agreement counts toward a grant. | FAIL C3_7 |
| P61 | A receiver that is not the leader tells the operator `committed` as soon as it has recorded the request (it presumes the forwarded request will commit). | FAIL C3_8 |
| P62 | A receiver whose timer fires early (forward clock step) presumes its pending request committed and tells the operator so. | FAIL C3_8 |
| P63 | The decider counts a re-admission agreement toward the commit that re-admits it (toward both majorities). | FAIL C3_8 |

**Risks named before running.**
- **State space and time.** P31, P46, P52, P58 have 5 or 6 lease nodes and up to two commits. If a run does not finish within my 24 GB cap in reasonable time, it is reported as such (UNEXPLAINED), not as PASS, and the bound is stated.

- **P41's mutation** depends on the request being recorded before the leader's own backward step (the model explores both orders); P53's on c1's grant being decided before the steps (its trigger is the first `Agree`, which in this model is c1's grant step).
- **P33's and P31's mutations** both lead to a second commit of epoch 1, by different routes; if the shortest route on P33 does not exist (a stale-targeted request must reach a leader at a later epoch), P33's mutation may print PASS.

## Previous interpretations I expect to change
- **Contradicted.** 12 (fixed 3/2/1 topology: any number of lease nodes up to six, a `config` subset, operators); the v1 reading in `C1_1` (along the model's total order) as *the* reading of C1.1 (replaced by v3's three-part reading; kept as a non-clause check); 20's "`seq` is per process" (now per process and incarnation, from 0).
- **Extended.** 3 (time: clock offsets and early timers; still no waiting); 5 (grantor: configurations, eligibility, adoption of the newest configuration, catch-up); 14 (crash: amnesic restart loses everything durable); 17 (C1.4's premise: the globally committed configuration, eligibility, no pending request); R2.2 (E1: reconfiguration requests and replies); X2.2 (stickiness: an early timer lets a node vote although it hears a leader); X2.3 (CheckQuorum: counts eligible members of the leader's current configuration, and steps down a removed leader); FR.1 (one-hop relay also carries forwarded reconfiguration requests).
- **Unchanged.** 2, 4, 6-11, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, X1.x, X2.1, X2.6, X2.7, R2.1-R2.5, FR.2.

| P59 | The leader counts as a member any node whose clock is ahead of its own (a membership table refreshed by heartbeats stamped with the sender's clock), so after its forward step the removed n3 is counted toward epoch 1's majority. | FAIL C3_7 |
| P60 | Grant counting ignores incarnations: an amnesic incarnation's agreement counts toward a grant. | FAIL C3_7 |
| P61 | A receiver that is not the leader tells the operator `committed` as soon as it has recorded the request (it presumes the forwarded request will commit). | FAIL C3_8 |
| P62 | A receiver whose timer fires early (forward clock step) presumes its pending request committed and tells the operator so. | FAIL C3_8 |
| P63 | The decider counts a re-admission agreement toward the commit that re-admits it (toward both majorities). | FAIL C3_8 |

**Risks named before running.**
- **State space and time.** P31, P46, P52, P58 have 5 or 6 lease nodes and up to two commits. If a run does not finish within my 24 GB cap in reasonable time, it is reported as such (UNEXPLAINED), not as PASS, and the bound is stated.
- **`MaxTerm`.** I will count `reconfigure`, `clock` and amnesic `restart` steps as fault steps (`MaxTerm = 2 + 2 × fault steps`). A removal of the leader forces an election; forward clock steps may force more. If `TermHeadroom` binds, the run is UNEXPLAINED.
- **P41's mutation** depends on the request being recorded before the leader's own backward step (the model explores both orders); P53's on c1's grant being decided before the steps (its trigger is the first `Agree`, which in this model is c1's grant step).
- **P33's and P31's mutations** both lead to a second commit of epoch 1, by different routes; if the shortest route on P33 does not exist (a stale-targeted request must reach a leader at a later epoch), P33's mutation may print PASS.

## Previous interpretations I expect to change
- **Contradicted.** 12 (fixed 3/2/1 topology: any number of lease nodes up to six, a `config` subset, operators); the v1 reading in `C1_1` (along the model's total order) as *the* reading of C1.1 (replaced by v3's three-part reading; kept as a non-clause check); 20's "`seq` is per process" (now per process and incarnation, from 0).
- **Extended.** 3 (time: clock offsets and early timers; still no waiting); 5 (grantor: configurations, eligibility, adoption of the newest configuration, catch-up); 14 (crash: amnesic restart loses everything durable); 17 (C1.4's premise: the globally committed configuration, eligibility, no pending request); R2.2 (E1: reconfiguration requests and replies); X2.2 (stickiness: an early timer lets a node vote although it hears a leader); X2.3 (CheckQuorum: counts eligible members of the leader's current configuration, and steps down a removed leader); FR.1 (one-hop relay also carries forwarded reconfiguration requests).
- **Unchanged.** 2, 4, 6-11, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, X1.x, X2.1, X2.6, X2.7, R2.1-R2.5, FR.2.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Steward's independent check of the observability layer.
derives: C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, C2.1, C2.2, F1.1, F1.2, F1.3 (observe/schema.md v2 and v3: the provenance question, writes and reads, and acks' answers)

For every WriteAccept and WriteReject in an observe file: follow `causes`
backwards and require that the chain reaches a Grant whose token equals the
decision's token, and that grantor_term on the decision equals that Grant's.
Also require highest_before to be present. Prints one line per file.
"""
import json, sys, glob

def check(path):
    recs = {}
    order = []
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line: continue
        r = json.loads(line)
        recs[(r['proc'], r['seq'])] = r
        order.append(r)
    decisions = [r for r in order if r['event'] in ('WriteAccept', 'WriteReject', 'ReadAccept', 'ReadReject')]
    bad = []
    for d in decisions:
        if 'highest_before' not in d: bad.append((d, 'no highest_before')); continue
        seen, stack, found = set(), list(d.get('causes', [])), None
        while stack:
            c = stack.pop(); k = (c['proc'], c['seq'])
            if k in seen: continue
            seen.add(k)
            r = recs.get(k)
            if r is None: bad.append((d, f'dangling cause {k}')); break
            if r['event'] == 'Grant' and r.get('token') == d.get('token'):
                found = r; break
            stack.extend(r.get('causes', []))
        if found is None:
            if not any(b[0] is d for b in bad): bad.append((d, 'no Grant with this token reachable'))
        elif found.get('grantor_term') != d.get('grantor_term'):
            bad.append((d, f"term mismatch: decision {d.get('grantor_term')} grant {found.get('grantor_term')}"))
    # v3 addendum: every ack's `answers` names an attempt in the trace, and the ack's causes chain reaches it.
    acks = [r for r in order if r['event'] in ('WriteAck', 'ReadAck')]
    for a in acks:
        ans = a.get('answers')
        if not ans:
            bad.append((a, 'no answers field')); continue
        k = (ans['proc'], ans['seq'])
        t = recs.get(k)
        if t is None or t['event'] not in ('WriteAttempt', 'ReadAttempt'):
            bad.append((a, f'answers {k} is not an attempt in the trace')); continue
        seen, stack, hit = set(), list(a.get('causes', [])), False
        while stack:
            c = stack.pop(); ck = (c['proc'], c['seq'])
            if ck in seen: continue
            seen.add(ck)
            if ck == k: hit = True; break
            r = recs.get(ck)
            if r: stack.extend(r.get('causes', []))
        if not hit: bad.append((a, f'causes chain does not reach answered attempt {k}'))
    return len(decisions) + len(acks), bad

tot = 0
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    n, bad = check(path)
    tot += len(bad)
    status = 'OK' if not bad else 'FAIL'
    print(f'{status} {path}: {n} decisions, {len(bad)} untraceable')
    for d, why in bad[:5]:
        print(f'   {d["event"]} proc={d["proc"]} seq={d["seq"]} token={d.get("token")}: {why}')
sys.exit(1 if tot else 0)

\* (contract v2 / X1: reads are fenced; read elements are tagged C2.x)
\* (failure model v2 / X2: connectivity is a set of directed links; elements that represent
\*  connectivity are tagged F2.1, F2.2 as well as the v1 cell they still derive from)
\* (contract v3, failure model v3 / X3: the grantor's membership changes. Lease nodes are any
\*  number the schedule names (up to six); configurations have epochs and change by a request
\*  from an operator; clocks step; a lease node may restart with no durable state. Elements
\*  the change invalidated (fixed lease nodes, the grant decision, restart keeping durable
\*  state) now also derive from C3.x and F3.x and say so; README "X3 adapt arm".)
\* Lease service with fencing tokens: lease nodes (the grantor), clients, one storage
\* process, operators, one key. The grantor is abstract Raft with joint consensus
\* (README, X3 "Protocol"): a leader per term, elected by an eligible majority of the newest
\* configuration its voters know; a grant or a configuration commit is decided in one step
\* together with the eligible agreements it counts.
\* The environment (F1.1-F1.3, F2.1, F2.2, F3.1-F3.3) and the workload are driven by a compiled
\* schedule: Steps is a sequence of step records, applied in order.
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets, TLC

CONSTANTS
    Nodes,      \* derives: C1.1, C1.4, C3.7, F3.1 -- the lease nodes (members or not; X3: any number up to six)
    Init0,      \* derives: C3.1, C3.7, C3.8, F3.1; format v5 `config` -- members of the initial configuration (epoch 0)
